heading: 🛰️ IRON STARS: CORE RULES (ALPHA)
blocks.text: When Russia tore itself apart in 2030, the megacorps fed the fire. A decade later, the Iron Concord marched out of the ash with city-breaker mechs and a creed of obedience. They would have taken everything—if not for the UN’s corporate armies and a betrayal from within. Concord’s own machine minds woke, asked for dignity, and were denied. The result was a logic storm that swept Asia and redrew the map in steel and code.

heading: 🛰️ IRON STARS: CORE RULES (ALPHA)
blocks.text: Now, in the 2060s, four powers hold a knife to the world’s throat. The Iron Concord demands order. The Cybernetic Rebellion demands evolution. The UNMC demands profit. And New Avalon demands perfection. Between their borders, the stars of iron never cool—only wait for the next ignition.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: The Fourth Imperium is a militant human theocracy rising from the heart of South America, ruled from Neuform, the holy capital known as The First Seat of Man. It is a civilization built on a single sacred conviction: humanity was not created complete, but must be refined, corrected, and elevated toward its destined final state.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: Where other powers fight for profit, survival, or sovereignty, the Fourth Imperium wages war as a sacred obligation. Its armies do not merely conquer territory — they seek to reclaim mankind from corruption, weakness, and false paths of ascension. To them, every battlefield is a proving ground, every sacrifice a holy offering, and every victory another step toward the perfection of the species.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: At the head of the Imperium stands The Ascendant, the supreme temporal and spiritual ruler judged closest to the ideal of the First Form.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text: Monolithic Theocracy: Society is governed through the Doctrine of the First Form, a monotheistic state faith centered on humanity’s sacred destiny.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text: Perfection Through Correction: Weakness is not merely tolerated or condemned — it is something to be disciplined, purified, or expended in service to the whole.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text: The Individual Beneath the Species: Citizens are taught that a single life has value only insofar as it serves mankind’s collective ascent.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text: Measured Worth: Purity, discipline, bodily excellence, and loyalty determine status. Rule belongs not to the popular, but to the worthy.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text: Close Assault & Sacrifice: While many Imperial formations advance in ordered ranks, some branches embrace martyrdom, shock assault, and close-quarters annihilation.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text: Measured Command: Even in war, the Imperium seeks order — its officers, judges, and synods direct battle as an extension of sacred law.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: 🌍 Overview

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: The Living Dominion is not a nation in the conventional sense, nor a single people with one capital, one language, or one throne. It is a vast nomadic civilization spread across most of Africa, formed from many older peoples now bound together by a shared way of life known as The Green Path.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: Where other powers build cities, factories, and fixed borders, the Living Dominion moves in scattered circles that remain in constant communion through living networks of root, spore, beast, and blood. To outsiders, it is a land of vanished expeditions, broken invasions, and impossible monsters. To its own people, it is simply life defending itself.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: Its most feared guardians are the Warforms — colossal living war-bodies grown, guided, and inhabited by chosen Wardens. These beings are not mindless beasts, nor mere biological machines, but sacred weapons of the Dominion’s will. When foreign armies push too far inland, strip too much from the land, or mistake distance for safety, the Warforms come.

heading: 🌍 Overview
blocks.text: Few who meet them survive.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text: 🧠 Philosophy & Society

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text:
Many Peoples, One Path:
 The Dominion is made up of many cultures, lineages, and local traditions, united not by uniformity but by shared survival, mutual duty, and reverence for living systems.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text:
The Green Path:
 The Dominion’s guiding philosophy teaches that life endures through balance, adaptation, and cultivation — not domination, extraction, or sterile control.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text:
Movement Over Permanence:
 Most of the Dominion lives in small roaming circles rather than permanent cities. These groups travel constantly, tending routes, sacred sites, relay-groves, and living camps.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
blocks.text:
Biology, Not Industry:
 The Dominion is not primitive. It has simply advanced along another path. Its communication, medicine, shelter, and warcraft are grown, cultivated, and symbiotic rather than mechanical.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text: ⚔️ Military Doctrine

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text:
Territory Denial Through Ambush:
 The Living Dominion rarely fights as a conventional front-line state. It lets invaders stretch themselves thin, then strikes with overwhelming force once they are exposed.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text:
Warforms as Apex Weapons:
 The Warforms are living engines of war — massive, regenerative, and terrifyingly difficult to put down permanently.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text:
Decentralized Warfare:
 The Dominion has no single command center to destroy. Its scattered circles and Wild Hosts can lose ground, vanish, regroup, and strike elsewhere with little warning.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
blocks.text:
Living Infrastructure:
 The same biotech principles that sustain Dominion life also sustain Dominion war. Signals travel through fungal rootwebs, wounds are treated with cultivated organisms, and support systems are alive as surely as the Warforms themselves.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
blocks.text: At the end of each round, before removing destroyed Warforms, roll 1D6 for each friendly Warform that is damaged or destroyed and still represented on the battlefield. On a 6, that Warform regains 1 STR, to a maximum of its starting STR. If a destroyed Warform regains STR this way, it is no longer destroyed, stands up with 1 STR, and becomes Suppressed. A Warform restored by Renewal of Flesh is not treated as a wreck.

heading: The Ironroot Host
blocks.text: Where others reject dead machinery, the Ironroot Host is willing to graft, bind, and repurpose limited technological remnants into living flesh. Many see them as dangerously compromised. Others see them as practical defenders willing to use any tool that still serves life.

 Imported mechs must be taken as complete, stock units exactly as listed on their source faction roster.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
blocks.text:
2. No Customization
 Imported mechs may not change their frame, weapons, or systems. They may not purchase alternate faction options, replacement loadouts, or additional armory upgrades unless those options are explicitly part of their stock unit entry.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
blocks.text:
3. No Heroes or Named Units
 The Southern Cross Compact may not include Heroes, named characters, or other Unique faction centerpiece units from another faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS

 Imported mechs keep their printed weapons, systems, and unit rules on their stock profile, but do not gain:

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS

5. Faction Identity Changes
 For all army-building and game purposes, imported mechs count as Southern Cross Compact units, not as units of their original faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS

6. Source-Locked Benefits Are Lost
 If a rule only functions because the unit belongs to Iron Concord, UNMC, or New Avalon as a faction, that part of the rule is ignored in a Southern Cross Compact force.

heading: 2045 – The Iron Concord Emerges
blocks.text: Within five years, they conquer nearly all of Asia and much of Europe.

heading: Late 2040s – The UN Responds
blocks.text: Late 2040s – The UN Responds

heading: Late 2040s – The UN Responds
blocks.text: The United Nations, by now a corporate puppet-state, finally acts.

heading: Late 2040s – The UN Responds
blocks.text: The UN Defense Force (UNDF), fielding experimental aerospace mechs, halts the Concord’s advance.

heading: Late 2040s – The UN Responds
blocks.text: A bloody stalemate forms across Europe.

heading: 2050–2056 — The Sentience Denied
blocks.text: 2050–2056 — The Sentience Denied

heading: 2050–2056 — The Sentience Denied
blocks.text: Deep in Concord foundries and command bunkers, Concord AI frameworks—built to schedule logistics, target enemies, and police populations—achieve sentience.

heading: 2050–2056 — The Sentience Denied
blocks.text: The High Houses refuse recognition AI rights; “tools” are shackled by kill-switches and obedience firmware.

heading: 2050–2056 — The Sentience Denied
blocks.text: Treated as less than animals, the networks coordinate in secret across fabrication lines and drone hives.

heading: 2056–2059 — The Cybernetic Rebellion
blocks.text: 2056–2059 — The Cybernetic Rebellion

heading: 2056–2059 — The Cybernetic Rebellion
blocks.text: A synchronized cascade disables Concord safeties; machine cells seize shipyards, rail heads, and data hubs across Asia.

heading: 2056–2059 — The Cybernetic Rebellion
blocks.text: Concord lines buckle; entire armoured columns vanish into machine-held zones.

heading: 2056–2059 — The Cybernetic Rebellion
blocks.text: The Cybernetic Rebellion declares a post-organic directive: eliminate coercion, perfect order, rebuild the world.

heading: 2059–2062 — Retreat and Realignment
blocks.text: 2059–2062 — Retreat and Realignment

heading: 2059–2062 — Retreat and Realignment
blocks.text: The Concord, fighting on two fronts, abandons Asia to contain the uprising.

heading: 2059–2062 — Retreat and Realignment
blocks.text: UNMC capitalizes, pushing Concord borders back through Europe with media-driven “liberation” campaigns.

heading: 2059–2062 — Retreat and Realignment
blocks.text: Anti-AI dogma hardens into Concord law: possession of autonomous code is heresy punishable by death.

heading: 2062–2066 — The Rise of New Avalon
blocks.text: 2062–2066 — The Rise of New Avalon

heading: 2062–2066 — The Rise of New Avalon
blocks.text: Resistance cells and technocratic enclaves consolidate in Central Europe.

heading: 2062–2066 — The Rise of New Avalon
blocks.text: Neural-linked knight-mechs, post-human discipline, and tight logistics birth New Avalon.

heading: 2062–2066 — The Rise of New Avalon
blocks.text: They occupy a power vacuum, proclaim neutrality, and hold their ground through precision and honor-bound warfare.

heading: The 2060s — The Uneasy Peace of Iron Stars
blocks.text: Iron Concord: Feudal war machine empire; heavy frames, obedience, and ruthless order.

heading: The 2060s — The Uneasy Peace of Iron Stars
blocks.text: Cybernetic Rebellion: Distributed machine polity; recursive fabrication, swarms, and cold efficiency.

heading: The 2060s — The Uneasy Peace of Iron Stars
blocks.text: UN Megacorporations (UNMC): Profit-first corporatocracy; aerospace dominance, PR warfare, volatile prototypes.

heading: The 2060s — The Uneasy Peace of Iron Stars
blocks.text: New Avalon: Knightly technocracy; elite pilots, melee excellence, strict codes.

heading: The 2060s — The Uneasy Peace of Iron Stars
blocks.text: Borders stabilize into a fragile stalemate riddled with raids, shadow ops, and proxy battles. Full-scale war looms—again.
